Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

# Conservative Party Manifesto 2015: Summary

## A Plan for Every Stage of Life

The Conservative Party presents a comprehensive vision centered on economic responsibility, individual empowerment, and national security. After five years of turning Britain around from Labour's "Great Recession," the Conservatives argue they are the only party capable of securing continued prosperity.

## Economic Foundation

The manifesto's core premise is that a strong economy underpins everything else. The Conservatives claim credit for transforming Britain from economic chaos into the fastest-growing major advanced economy. Their commitment is to eliminate the deficit, run a surplus by 2018-19, and begin paying down national debt—framed as both economic prudence and moral responsibility to future generations.

Key fiscal promises include: raising the tax-free Personal Allowance to £12,500, increasing the 40p threshold to £50,000, and committing to no increases in VAT, National Insurance, or Income Tax. The party pledges to find £30 billion in consolidation through departmental savings, £12 billion in welfare reform, and £5 billion from tackling tax evasion.

## Jobs and Enterprise

The manifesto celebrates creating 1.9 million jobs and sets an ambition for "full employment"—the highest employment rate of any major economy. Policies include three million new apprenticeships, abolishing employers' National Insurance for under-21s, and maintaining the most competitive business tax regime in the G20. A major review of business rates and continued support for small businesses through the Employment Allowance feature prominently.

The party commits to rebalancing the economy geographically, building a "Northern Powerhouse" with £13 billion in transport investment, and devolving powers to elected metro mayors.

## Welfare and Tax Reform

Central to the Conservative vision is rewarding work over welfare dependency. The manifesto promises a "Tax-Free Minimum Wage" through legislation ensuring no one working 30 hours on minimum wage pays Income Tax. The household benefit cap would reduce from £26,000 to £23,000, Universal Credit would continue rolling out, and 18-21 year-olds would face tougher requirements including a time-limited Youth Allowance.

Working families would receive 30 hours of free childcare for three and four-year-olds, alongside tax-free childcare worth up to £2,000 per child annually.

## Immigration Control

The Conservatives maintain their ambition for net migration in the "tens of thousands." Key proposals include requiring EU migrants to work and contribute for four years before claiming tax credits or child benefit, ending child benefit payments for children living abroad, introducing a four-year residency requirement for social housing, and removing jobseeking benefits for EU migrants entirely.

## Education and Skills

Every failing and coasting secondary school would become an academy. The party pledges 500 new free schools, protection for school funding, and the pupil premium. Rigorous standards include expectations that all 11-year-olds know times tables and perform complex multiplication, with resits for those who don't meet standards.

University places would have their cap removed, and a new postgraduate loan system would be introduced.

## National Health Service

The NHS receives particular emphasis, with commitments to increase spending by at least £8 billion above inflation by 2020, implement a seven-day NHS, guarantee same-day GP appointments for over-75s, and continue investment in cancer treatment and dementia research. The party frames itself as protector of the NHS while promising greater efficiency and transparency.

## Housing

The manifesto sets an ambition to double first-time buyers, building 200,000 Starter Homes at 20% below market price for under-40s. Help to Buy would extend, a new Help to Buy ISA would provide government top-ups on savings, and Right to Buy would extend to Housing Association tenants. Green Belt protection is pledged alongside brownfield development prioritization.

## Pensioners and Retirement

The triple lock on state pensions would continue, guaranteeing increases of at least 2.5%, inflation, or earnings growth. A new Single-Tier Pension would effectively abolish means-testing for lifelong contributors. Inheritance Tax reform would raise the effective threshold for couples to £1 million through a transferable main residence allowance.

## Constitutional Reform

The manifesto promises English votes for English laws, implementing the Smith Commission for Scotland, and further Welsh devolution. The Human Rights Act would be scrapped and replaced with a British Bill of Rights, breaking the formal link with the European Court of Human Rights.

## Europe

The defining commitment is an in-out referendum on EU membership by end of 2017, preceded by renegotiation of Britain's terms. The Conservatives want reform: less bureaucracy, an end to "ever closer union," and protection of British interests whether inside or outside the Eurozone.

## Defence and Security

Military spending would meet NATO's 2% target, the nuclear deterrent would be maintained with four new Successor submarines, and the Armed Forces Covenant would be honored. Counter-terrorism powers would strengthen, including new communications data legislation, while "Banning Orders" and "Extremism Disruption Orders" would target non-violent extremism.

## International Development

The 0.7% aid commitment would continue, targeting goals including immunizing 76 million children, educating 11 million children, and helping 60 million access clean water by 2020.

## Conclusion

The manifesto presents a coherent Conservative worldview: fiscal discipline enables public service investment; individual responsibility and hard work should be rewarded; welfare should provide a safety net, not a lifestyle; strong borders and controlled immigration protect British workers; and national security requires military strength and constitutional sovereignty. The underlying message is continuity—staying the course on the "long-term economic plan" rather than risking Labour's "economic chaos."
